It integrates\\nclassical convolutional neural networks with variational quantum\\ncircuits so that both quantum computing and deep learning can be used in\\ndecentralized, privacy-preserving environments. The functioning of the\\nFederated Learning model includes a efficient optimization algorithm\\nsuitable for quantum environments in FL called SCAFFOLD, which handle\\nclient heterogeneity and non-IID data distributions modeled using\\nDirichlet sampling. The framework includes three ways of training normal\\ntraining along with trigger-based and semantic-based backdoor attacks to\\nunderstand demonstrating the susceptibility of federated skin cancer\\nmodels to stealthy adversarial behaviors. To defend against such\\nthreats, multiple detection and mitigation strategies are evaluated,\\nincluding Activation Clustering, Neural Cleanse, and Fine-Pruning. .\\nAdditionally, a novel approach for defense, Spectral Defense, is\\nproposed and developed, based on the eigen-spectrum analysis of internal\\nneural activations to detect and ultimately suppress backdoor behavior\\nwithout recourse to clean validation data. Experimental results on this\\nhybrid quantum-classical model prove improvement in classification\\nperformance, whereas the Spectral Defense framework provides significant\\nattack success rates reduction with little degradation in model\\naccuracy. This work provides a robust and scalable approach for\\ndeploying secure federated learning systems to adverse conditions for\\nmedical image analysis.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.22541/au.174731423.33892933/v1\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 5, 15]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1007/s44464-026-00025-9\", \"title\": [\"Representational efficiency and noise robustness in hybrid qu…
